title: Longitudinal Back Stroking
summary: A gentle foundational technique in which both palms glide from the lower back toward the shoulders.
goal: Prepare the soft tissues for subsequent techniques while creating warmth and relaxation.
imageAlt: Educational diagram of longitudinal back stroking without text labels.
startingPosition: The person lies face down. Place both palms on the lower back on either side of the spine.
instructions: Place both palms gently on the lower back.
Glide both palms upward over the muscles on either side of the spine.
Near the upper back, gently move the hands outward.
Return down along the sides using minimal pressure.
direction: Primary movement: lower back to shoulders; return gently along the sides.
tips: Keep the movement symmetrical and unhurried.
mistakes: Strong direct pressure on the spine.
warning: Do not perform this technique over acute pain, recent injury, significant inflammation, damaged skin, or when touch increases symptoms. Seek qualified professional advice when uncertain.
